Another thing you are overlooking is cost. It is not $1000 for a commercial; form my experience the cheapest I have seen is around $2000 for the commercial plus you need the actors, set, writers, and crew so add another $10,000. Next you need to get the targeted markets from polling which is something the campaign already has broken down by districts and you target districts where he has low name recognition and a high undecided or a low name recognition or platform recognition and Clinton has lost ground and that ground has gone back to being undecided.

The other option would be to run a statewide or national commercial campaign which would be very much out of your reach - sorry its true.

Next, you need the media relations guys to go out and get the TV commercials on the air and pay for them. You will have to pay per commercial, per minute, and the price varies based on how many people are watching that show - often indexed with Neilson numbers or a similar system.

So lets say that ad campaign in one New Hampshire district ran with ten commercials a day for ten days:

Item Quantity Cost Total
Commercial Minute 100 $3000 $300,000
Filming Expenses 1 $10,000 $310,000
Public Relations Specialist 1 $6000 $316,000
Total $316,000

Now in a small state like New Hampshire you can also get multiple districts within a single media market - a city for example - but I only used New Hampshire because that is relevant and timely.

The problem you are going to run into is raising that $316,000 for every, single, individual media market that you are targeting ads in.
